 Live .  954 viewing 954 viewing Live page Updated 11 minutes ago First Eurovision Asia under way as world's biggest song contest heads to Bangkok
 Summary
 All eleven acts have performed in the first ever Eurovision Song Contest Asia
 Voting is already open, here's how you can cast yours 
 On stage, we saw a performance from a beatboxing collective, a number of ballads and a pop song called BAE - here's a recap 
 Eurovision Asia has been talked about for two decades, but never materialised - until now, our correspondent in Bangkok writes 
 Close form Who do you want to win?
 Get in touch Live Reporting
 Edited by Matt Spivey, with Jonathan Head reporting from the One Bangkok Forum
 It's time for Dara's Bangaranga published at 15:09 GMT 15:09 GMT 
 Image source, Jonathan Head/COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU Image caption, Reigning Eurovision champion Dara on stage
 Eurovision winner Dara is now performing her hit song Bangaranga - which made her, and Bulgaria, the champion of this year's Song Contest. 
 She is also performing her new hit single Bad Idea on stage.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Outfits underwent huge changes in run-up to contest published at 15:08 GMT 15:08 GMT 
 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 Image source, Ralph Larmann/COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU Image caption, Bhutan's Nyendra performed his folk-pop entry in a traditional outfit
 A big part of Eurovision is the vocals - but the outfits also have a part to play in the performances.
 Most of the costumes for this final have undergone big changes, except for that of Bhutan's Nyendra. 
 He stuck to his country's national dress, the gho.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 A technical error leads to a second showing of BAE published at 15:05 GMT 15:05 GMT 
 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 Oops... They have just played the music video for BAE - the entry from Laos' Thinla - over an apparent technical issue in the live show.
 This means Thinla's catchy ditty is the last song the audience will hear.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Ready to vote? Here's how published at 15:04 GMT 15:04 GMT 
 The winner of the Eurovision Song Contest Asia will perform on stage at Eurovision 2027 in Bulgaria.
 Have you decided who you want to vote for? Here's how to have your say:
 You can vote from anywhere in the world - just access the vote on the website , external .
 Each person gets eight votes free - but the rules stipulate you must distribute your points among a minimum of three songs.
 You can purchase ten extra votes.
 Viewers cannot vote for their own country - as is the case in the Eurovision Song Contest.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 All eleven acts have performed - a recap published at 15:01 GMT 15:01 GMT 
 Image source, Jonathan Head/COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU Image caption, Acts from the final on their feet at the end of Aina Abul's performance
 That's a wrap on the eleven performances at the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia.
 Here's a recap:
 Vietnam's Tóc Tiên started off strong with slick choreogaphy, backing dancers and an elaborate fairy-like get-up
 Monetrey from Cambodia then dialled things back, performing an ambitious ballad alone on stage under a single spotlight
 Thinla from Laos followed up with the crowd-pleasing Bae, opting to perform in a vibrant, traditional Lao hilltribe outfit
 Mongolian crooner Beck then brought the drama with a heartfelt performance of Chamguigeer (Without You)
 Backed by a duo performing a romantic interpretive dance sequence, Nyendra from Bhutan showed off his impressive pipes with the folk-pop tune Lhayi Semo
 Carmelle from the Phillipines then launched into Sobra-Sobra - blending vocals with a unexpectedly delightful rap verse
 The beatboxing Bangladeshi group Beatmosphere eschewed the traditional backing track, instead using their voices to replicate the sounds of drums and basslines
 Thailand's MANG x DAOU brought the harmonies, eliciting huge cheers from the home crowd for their emotive duet
 JUNHEE of South Korea brought a slick K-pop number, and the crowd went wild when he took off his jacket
 For Nepal , Pratik Himal Rai made good use of his staging, with a fiery backdrop for his performance
 And finally, Malaysia's Ania Abdul closed the show with her powerful vocals - the other acts were on their feet as she ended

 Some Eurovision Asia trivia... published at 14:53 GMT 14:53 GMT 
 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 As the show is closing, here's a fun fact for you.
 Both Carmelle from the Philippines and Aina Abdul from Malaysia (who is on stage now) won awards at the World Championships of Performing Arts in California - a competition set up to showcase global talent - in 2019 and 2014 respectively.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Malaysia's Aina Abdul closing the show published at 14:52 GMT 14:52 GMT 
 Image source, Eurovision Song Contest Asia It's time for the last performance of the night... Malaysia's Aina Abdul.
 The singer-songwriter and actress has represented Malaysia on an international stage before, at the World Championship of Performing Arts in 2014.
 She also dressed as the country's national flower to compete on The Masked Singer Malaysia which she won.
 She will be singing Bluest Sky - the song demands powerful vocals and plenty of emotion, let's see how she does.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 The staging has been amazing published at 14:50 GMT 14:50 GMT 
 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 Image source, COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU Pratik Himal Rai from Nepal made good use of the screens and lights here at the One Bangkok Forum Arena.
 There were a lot of worries among Eurovision fans about how good the staging would be here in Thailand, especially after the $1m dollar budget cut last month stopped experienced Eurovision technicians from coming. 
 But the lighting and effects have been amazing.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Just one act left to go... and there's plenty of dancing on the sidelines published at 14:48 GMT 14:48 GMT 
 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 Image source, COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU One act to go, and contestants who have already performed are watching from the sofas on one side of the venue and dancing to the other acts.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 A predictably slick K-pop number from JUNHEE published at 14:43 GMT 14:43 GMT 
 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 Back to JUNHEE's performance.
 It was a predictably slick K-pop number, the biggest cheer came when he tore off his jacket.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 'Endless love' from Nepal - the penultimate act published at 14:41 GMT 14:41 GMT 
 Image source, Eurovision Song Contest Asia Pratik Himal Rai beat out 10 other acts on Nepal Decides to represent his country at Eurovision Asia. 
 He's appeared on several Nepalese TV shows and shot to fame after competing on the sixth season of The Voice of Nepal.
 Ananta Maya is the name of the song he'll be performing, which roughly translates as Endless Love. It's a unique mix of slow rock, Nepali folk and pop with some pretty fiery staging.
 And time for the penultimate act of the show.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 A 'deep dive' into the music styling of JUNHEE published at 14:39 GMT 14:39 GMT 
 Image source, Eurovision Song Contest Asia JUNHEE's Deep Dive is up next. 
 He's representing South Korea with his dance-y number with a rock-edge.
 The singer-songwriter has also been balancing his music with a new job - becoming the CEO of his own agency.
 Can his executive skills help him execute his track perfectly? We'll see.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 A Thai duet - made especially for Eurovision Asia published at 14:33 GMT 14:33 GMT 
 Image source, Eurovision Song Contest Asia/COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU Time for a duet.
 Thailand's MANG x DAOU - both solo artists outside of Eurovision Asia - have joined forces for this performance.
 They were greeted with huge cheers from the home crowd when they were introduced on stage in Bangkok.
 Emotions run high in this number, with plenty of harmonies.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Beatmosphere bring stronger beat to stage published at 14:28 GMT 14:28 GMT 
 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 Beatmosphere from Bangladesh have just finished their song Tumi Ele. 
 It has changed a lot since rehearsals, with a much stronger beat and intense red-lit backdrop.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Beatboxing Bangladeshi group up now published at 14:24 GMT 14:24 GMT 
 Image source, Ralph Larmann/COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU Image caption, Beatmosphere laying down their vocals at the rehearsals
 Beatboxing and a cappella, you say? Why not. It is Eurovision after all. 
 Beatmosphere are a collective who originally formed and bring something different to tonight's other acts - no backing track. 
 Tumi Ele, which they're performing, is a masterclass in how a blend of human voices - using harmonies and replicating the sound of drums and basslines - can produce everything needed for a fully-rounded song.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Many of the contestants are showbiz veterans published at 14:23 GMT 14:23 GMT 
 Jonathan Head 
South East Asia correspondent, at the One Bangkok Forum 
 Many of these contestants are experienced performers. Toc Tien from Vietnam has been in the business for 30 years, since she was a child. In Vietnam, she’s a mega celebrity. 
 Aina Abdul from Malaysia is also a huge star at home.
 When she was a child, Carmelle from the Philippines performed on the The Voice Kids. Since then, she's won talent competition show Tawag ng Tanghalan and even appeared on Pinoy Big Brother.
 As a reminder, the vote is now open - here's a reminder of how to cast yours. 
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Eurovision winner Dara graces the stage, as game show begins... published at 14:21 GMT 14:21 GMT 
 Bulgarian pop star Dara - the champion of this year's Eurovision - is now on stage. 
 She's going to give us an extra-special version of Bangaranga", her winning song, during the grand final. 
 We're then shown a look ahead to Bulgaria's 2027 Eurovision Song Contest - as three fans are given the chance to win tickets to see the final. 
 Suddenly, Eurovision Song Contest Asia has turned into a game show...
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 This song is a female empowerment anthem, says Sobra-Sobra writer published at 14:15 GMT 14:15 GMT 
 Matt and Nika, who wrote and produced the Philippines entry Sobra-Sobra, tell the BBC that they're "very excited and nervous" about the performance.
 "We can't believe it's happening right now," Matt says.
 The song is a women's empowerment anthem, Nika explains. "The song really says you can be whoever you want to be," she says. 
 They add they're "lucky" that Carmelle will be performing the song. 
 "She's so professional," Matt says, while Nika adds that she "embodies" the song. 
 Filipinos love music, they both say, so they're confident that Eurovision could be a big success there.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Has Philippines' Carmelle 'figured it out'? published at 14:14 GMT 14:14 GMT 
 Image source, Eurovision Song Contest Asia/COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU Image caption, Carmelle in rehearsals for her performance
 An anthem of owning your own femininity is up next in the form of a pop ballad, with an impressive rap section.
 It's Carmelle - who has appeared in Pinoy Big Brother and was runner-up on The Voice Kids - representing the Philippines. 
 Her official biography on the Eurovision Asia website says her music career has "skyrocketed to new heights in recent years".
 In her song Sobra-Sobra, she says "I have figured it out" - but let's see if she's worked out how to win the competition.
 Share close panel Share page Copy link About sharing 
 Can Bhutan's bilingual vocalist clinch a win? published at 14:09 GMT 14:09 GMT 
 Image source, Ralph Larmann/COURTESY OF VOXOVATION AND EBU Image caption, Nyendra performing at this year's rehearsals
 Bhutan's song Lhayi Semo - from folk-pop star Nyendra - was the first song to be announced for the inaugural Eurovision Song Contest Asia.
 The 24-year-old artist, who holds university degree in journalism and writes and produces his own songs, beat four other artists in a national competition to represent Bhutan. 
 Nyendra's music spans several genres - and languages, he performs his songs in both English and Dzongkha. 
 Let's see how his performance goes.
